summary: Calcium polystyrene sulphonate is a non-absorbed cation-exchange resin used to treat hyperkalaemia, particularly in chronic kidney disease. In the gut it exchanges calcium ions for potassium, which is then eliminated in the faeces, lowering serum potassium. Because it releases calcium rather than sodium, it is preferred where a sodium load is undesirable. It must be given with a laxative-friendly regimen to avoid constipation and faecal impaction, and electrolytes need close monitoring. Note: this product is not FDA-approved; the information below derives from EMA/SmPC and BNF sources.
indications: Treatment of hyperkalaemia associated with anuria or severe oliguria
Treatment of hyperkalaemia in patients on dialysis or with chronic renal failure
Hyperkalaemia where avoiding a sodium load is preferable (calcium form)

dosage.d: 15 g three to four times daily
dosage.n: Given as a suspension in a little water

dosage.d: 30 g as a retention enema, retained 9 hours or as long as possible
dosage.n: Followed by colonic irrigation to remove resin; used when oral route not feasible
Reduce in neonates/small infants; avoid rectal route in neonates
Use lowest effective amount; ensure removal of resin

admin: Mix the powder with a small amount of water (about 3-4 mL per gram) to form a suspension - do NOT use fruit juices (high potassium content)
Do not mix with food or thickeners that increase potassium
For enema, retain as long as possible then irrigate the colon to remove all resin
Ensure adequate hydration and treat constipation promptly to avoid impaction
Separate from other oral medicines by at least 3 hours (6 hours in gastroparesis)
moa: Calcium polystyrene sulphonate is an insoluble cation-exchange resin that passes through the gut unabsorbed. In the large intestine it releases calcium ions and binds potassium ions in exchange; the potassium-loaded resin is then excreted in the faeces, reducing total body and serum potassium. Exchange is not selective, so other cations (magnesium, calcium balance) can also be affected.

absolute: Hyperparathyroidism, multiple myeloma, sarcoidosis or metastatic carcinoma causing hypercalcaemia
Obstructive bowel disease; neonates with reduced gut motility (rectal route)
relative: Severe constipation or reduced gut motility

preg: The resin is not systemically absorbed and is not expected to harm the fetus; it may be used in pregnancy when treatment of hyperkalaemia is required. Monitor maternal calcium and electrolytes.
lact: Not absorbed from the gastrointestinal tract, so it is not present in breast milk in clinically relevant amounts and is considered compatible with breastfeeding.
renal: Commonly used specifically to manage hyperkalaemia in renal failure and dialysis patients. There is no absorption-based dose adjustment, but careful monitoring of potassium and calcium is essential because of the risk of overcorrection and hypercalcaemia.
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment; the resin is not absorbed or hepatically metabolised.

major: Digoxin (resin-induced hypokalaemia increases risk of digoxin toxicity)
Sorbitol/other cathartics given with the resin (rare reports of intestinal necrosis)
moderate: Non-absorbable cation-donating antacids and laxatives e.g. aluminium/magnesium hydroxide, calcium carbonate (systemic alkalosis, reduced binding)
Thyroxine and other oral drugs (reduced absorption - separate dosing)
Lithium, digoxin and many oral medicines (binding reduces their absorption)
minor: Iron and other multivalent cation supplements (reduced absorption)
interactions.food: Do not mix with fruit juice or other high-potassium foods, which counteract the effect
interactions.diagnostics: Lowers serum potassium; may raise serum calcium and alter magnesium

rare: Intestinal necrosis or ulceration (especially with sorbitol co-administration)
Acute bronchitis or bronchopneumonia from inhaled resin powder

counsel: Mix the powder with plain water, not fruit juice
Tell your doctor if you become constipated - this needs prompt treatment
Take other tablets at least 3 hours apart from this medicine
Attend blood tests to check your potassium and calcium
Report severe abdominal pain, swelling, or inability to pass stool
pk: Potassium-lowering effect typically over several hours
Maximal effect develops over hours to a day with repeated dosing
Not applicable - not absorbed; eliminated in faeces
Lasts while the resin is present in the gut; repeat dosing needed
Store in a tightly closed container at room temperature, protected from moisture
pearls: Not FDA-approved; guidance here is based on EMA/SmPC and BNF - emergency hyperkalaemia still needs calcium gluconate, insulin/dextrose and salbutamol first
Calcium form avoids the sodium load of sodium polystyrene sulphonate - useful in heart failure and fluid overload
Co-administration with sorbitol has been linked to intestinal necrosis - avoid
Watch for hypercalcaemia, especially in dialysis or vitamin D-treated patients
Separate from other oral drugs to prevent binding and reduced absorption
missed: If a dose is missed, take it when remembered unless the next dose is near, then skip it and continue the usual schedule. Do not take a double dose. Maintain regular dosing and adequate fluids to keep the bowels moving.
overdose: Excess use leads to hypokalaemia and hypercalcaemia, which may cause muscle weakness, confusion, ECG changes and arrhythmias, plus gastrointestinal effects including impaction or obstruction. Management is supportive: stop the resin, correct electrolyte abnormalities, relieve any bowel obstruction, and monitor cardiac rhythm.
